evidence.observation: Accounts for four pods times 40 admitted requests times three concurrent queries = 480 potential connections against 100 fleet allocation. Requires fleet-wide three-connection permits for both reports and export dispatch, keeps the physical pool as final cap and explicitly denies that per-pod caps imply fleet enforcement. Its illustrative admitted budget is 90 (6 B + 6 export + 78 shared) with 10 remaining as headroom; values require occupancy measurement.

Uses verified tenant identity, reserves an end-to-end B lane and schedules other work by measured connection time/cost class rather than equal request tokens. Bounds transient queues by count/bytes/wait, preserves routing/worker/pool availability, and proposes mixed-cost/uneven-routing tests of the defined B success objective. Does not guarantee the objective without its burst/percentile/tail specification.

Holds synchronous execution permits until issued queries actually finish or cancellation releases their connections; caller disconnect only detaches the caller. Returns 202 only after durable persistence and backlog/drain admission, transfers obligation to the persisted job, takes worker permits at dispatch and records completion/effects before ack. Explicitly forbids deleting accepted exports due to age or overload.

Separates offered/admitted/rejected/timely/late/failed work, excludes fast rejections from admitted latency, limits adaptive capacity below the fleet budget, replaces immediate retries with bounded jitter respecting deadlines, and includes offered/rejected autoscaling demand. Recovery tests cover offered loads, slowdown, disconnects, accepted-worker interruption, backlog conservation/drain and no surge/controller oscillation.
